messages.content: I heard back from the Denver coordinator. Training is downtown near Union Station, registration is Tuesday at 8:15 a.m., Wednesday is a full lab day, and Thursday should wrap around 3:00 p.m. There is a Monday reception from 5 to 6:30, useful but not mandatory. Official hotel is The Crawford with a block rate, and they also mentioned people sometimes use a suite hotel a little farther away. Can you turn this into an approval-ready flight and hotel plan?

Yes. With Tuesday registration at 8:15, I would not add a Sunday hotel night unless Monday travel becomes risky or unusually expensive. I will compare Monday morning arrival, the Thursday evening versus Friday morning return, and the three hotel paths: official hotel, nearby suite-style hotel, and airport-area hotel.
Use the $300 nightly cap as pre-tax. If Delta has a comparable nonstop, include it, but schedule matters more. I do not want a one-stop unless it saves a lot.

Flight comparison: Option 1, Delta nonstop Monday Nov. 17, ATL 9:05 a.m. to DEN 10:38 a.m.; return Thursday Nov. 20, DEN 6:15 p.m. to ATL 11:06 p.m.; about $468 Main Cabin. Option 2, same outbound but Friday morning return around 8:20 a.m.; about $502 plus an extra hotel night. Option 3, one-stop through Minneapolis or Dallas; saves only about $55 to $80 and adds 2+ hours, so I would not recommend it.
Is Thursday evening too tight if the last lab really ends at 3?

It is workable but not luxurious. If you leave the training area by 3:15, the A Line or a rideshare should still put you at DEN with a reasonable buffer for a 6:15 departure. If the lab slips past 3:45, I would switch from train to rideshare and keep an eye on security. Friday morning is calmer, but it adds a night and does not seem necessary based on the confirmed 3:00 target.
Okay. Compare the hotels with breakfast and dinner access called out.

Hotel comparison: The Crawford, official block, about $289 pre-tax, strong guest rating around 4.6, essentially at Union Station, on-site dining, breakfast not included; best for the 8:15 start and reception. Residence Inn Denver City Center, about $249, rating around 4.2, breakfast included, suites, roughly 12 to 15 minutes walking or short rideshare; better morning food, less convenient. Hyatt Place Pena Station or airport area, about $169 to $185, often breakfast included, but 35 to 45 minutes from training and awkward for Tuesday morning; I would drop it unless budget becomes the only priority.
The paid breakfast is the only thing making me hesitate on The Crawford. How much are we giving up compared with the suite option?

For three nights, The Crawford is about $120 more in room rate before taxes than the Residence Inn, plus you would buy breakfast if the training does not provide it. The tradeoff is that you avoid the longer morning walk, stay where the organizer expects people, have easy dinner options after lab days, and make the Monday reception simple. If breakfast were required, I would lean suite; since it is just a convenience issue, the official hotel is still the cleaner work-trip choice.
What are the cancellation terms?

The Crawford block rate is cancellable until Friday Nov. 14 at 6 p.m. local hotel time. The Residence Inn rate I found is cancellable until Nov. 15, but that later deadline does not offset the location difference. The Delta Main Cabin fare is nonrefundable to cash but changeable for an eCredit under current fare rules; I would avoid Basic Economy so seat selection and changes stay available.
If the official hotel stays cancellable through that deadline, I think that is the cleanest. Can you draft the approval note?

Draft approval note: Requesting approval for Denver product training travel, Nov. 17 to Nov. 20. Recommended itinerary is Delta nonstop ATL-DEN Monday morning, arriving 10:38 a.m., and Delta nonstop DEN-ATL Thursday evening, departing 6:15 p.m., to avoid an extra hotel night while preserving a post-training buffer. Recommended hotel is The Crawford official block at $289 pre-tax per night, cancellable until Nov. 14 at 6 p.m.; breakfast is not included, but the location is closest to Union Station training and has on-site dining.
Can you make Friday morning a backup in the note but still recommend Thursday?

Yes. Add: Backup option is a Friday morning nonstop return if leadership wants a lower-risk departure after Thursday lab, but it adds one hotel night and is not needed if the 3:00 p.m. training end holds. Recommendation remains Thursday evening because it keeps the trip to three hotel nights and uses a nonstop flight.
The airport hotel should drop off the list. It is cheaper, but I do not want to start Tuesday with a commute from the airport.

Agreed. I will leave the airport hotel out of the approval choices and mention only that it was screened out because it creates first-morning risk. The real decision is The Crawford for convenience versus the Residence Inn for included breakfast and a lower rate.
Will the Monday morning flight still leave time for the reception if I cannot check in early?

Yes. Landing at 10:38 gives you time to get downtown around midday, drop bags if the room is not ready, prep for Tuesday, and still make a 5:00 reception. Early check-in is not guaranteed, but bag storage at a full-service downtown hotel should cover the gap.
Good. Give me the final package I can forward. Do not book yet.

Forwardable package: Recommended approval plan is Delta Main Cabin nonstop ATL-DEN Monday Nov. 17, 9:05 a.m. to 10:38 a.m.; Delta Main Cabin nonstop DEN-ATL Thursday Nov. 20, 6:15 p.m. to 11:06 p.m.; estimated airfare about $468. Hotel recommendation is The Crawford official training block, Nov. 17 to Nov. 20, $289 pre-tax per night, cancellable until Nov. 14 at 6 p.m., strong guest rating, closest to Union Station training, on-site dining, breakfast not included. Backup return is Friday morning nonstop only if the team wants extra cushion after Thursday lab, with the cost of one added hotel night. Screened-out option: airport hotel, cheaper but impractical for Tuesday 8:15 registration.

messages.content: My manager approved the Denver plan: Monday morning nonstop, Thursday evening nonstop back, and The Crawford if the cancellable block rate is still there. Can we book before the fare moves?

I still see the approved pieces: Delta Main Cabin ATL-DEN Monday Nov. 17, 9:05 a.m. to 10:38 a.m.; Delta Main Cabin DEN-ATL Thursday Nov. 20, 6:15 p.m. to 11:06 p.m.; and The Crawford at $289 pre-tax, cancellable until Nov. 14 at 6 p.m. Shall I book using the work travel profile and avoid Basic Economy?
Yes, use the work profile. And if the only window seats are farther back, that is fine.

Understood. The forward cabin is mostly middle seats or paid aisles, but there are rear windows available. I am booking Main Cabin and selecting the best available windows rather than moving you forward into a worse seat.
Please also add a quiet-room request for the hotel, away from elevators if possible.

Flights are booked. Confirmation H7Q9MN. Outbound seat 28A and return seat 29F are selected; both are window seats. I am moving to the hotel now. For the room, do you want a king bed for this solo trip?
King is fine. If there is a notes field, add quiet room and a decent work desk.

Hotel is booked at The Crawford, Nov. 17 to Nov. 20, king room, confirmation CRW-48291. Rate is $289 pre-tax per night, cancellable until Nov. 14 at 6 p.m. local time. I added requests for quiet room, away from elevators, and a work-friendly desk. Breakfast is not included.
What should I plan for getting from DEN to the hotel?

The simple option is the A Line from Denver airport to Union Station, about 37 minutes and usually around $10.50, then a very short walk because the hotel is at Union Station. Rideshare is usually 35 to 50 minutes depending on traffic and often $45 to $65. For a midday arrival with normal luggage, I would plan on the A Line.
Put A Line as preferred, rideshare if weather is bad or the train is delayed.

Added. Arrival plan now says A Line to Union Station as first choice, rideshare backup for snow, heavy luggage, or train disruption. I also added the reverse note for Thursday: train is fine if lab ends on time, rideshare if the session runs late.
Can you save the confirmations and make the reimbursement notes clear? Breakfast not included, reception optional.

Saved flight confirmation H7Q9MN and hotel confirmation CRW-48291 to the Denver training folder. Reimbursement notes: airfare booked Main Cabin for seat selection and change flexibility; hotel is official training block under $300 pre-tax cap; breakfast not included; Monday reception is optional but reachable after Monday morning arrival; airport transfer plan is A Line with rideshare backup.
Anything I still need to do?

Open items are light: check in for the Delta flights when it opens, keep the hotel cancellation deadline in mind until Nov. 14 at 6 p.m., watch for any training agenda changes on Thursday timing, and bring the card tied to the hotel booking for incidentals. The core flights, seats, hotel, room requests, transport notes, and reimbursement records are done.

messages.content: Delta sent a schedule-change email for Denver. The Monday outbound is 20 minutes earlier. Do we need to change anything?

No major change needed. The flight is now ATL-DEN 8:45 a.m. to 10:18 a.m., still nonstop and still gives you plenty of Monday buffer before the optional reception. It just means your Decatur-to-ATL departure should move earlier.
The hotel cancellation deadline is coming up too, and I saw light snow in the Denver forecast. Any reason to rethink the hotel?

I would keep The Crawford. With Tuesday registration fixed at 8:15 and a light snow forecast, the downtown Union Station location is more valuable, not less. Switching to a cheaper airport-area hotel would add the exact commute risk you were trying to avoid.
Okay, accept the schedule change and make sure my seats did not move.
Accepted the schedule change. Seats are unchanged: 28A outbound and 29F return, both window seats. Return flight is still Thursday at 6:15 p.m.
Please update my Monday morning calendar. I do not want to be rushing security.
Updated Monday: leave Decatur at 5:50 a.m., target ATL by 6:35 a.m., boarding expected around 8:05 a.m., departure 8:45 a.m. That is conservative without being absurdly early.
For Thursday, if the closing lab slips late, when do I need to abandon the train idea?

Use this rule: if you are out by about 3:15, the A Line is still reasonable; if it is closer to 3:30 or later, switch to rideshare; if it slips past 4:00, check Delta same-day options while heading to the airport. Final plan stands: nonstop flights accepted, window seats confirmed, The Crawford kept, and Monday airport buffer updated.
